name: Spanish Mosque (Bouzafar)
hero_subtitle: A hilltop walk to the best sunset view over the blue medina and the valley.

overview.title: The Viewpoint Everyone Climbs For
overview.p1: Bouzafar, better known as the Spanish Mosque, was built by the Spanish in the 1920s during the protectorate era and was never used for regular prayer. Its charm is the setting: a whitewashed mosque on a hill with a wide view over Chefchaouen and the mountains behind.
overview.p2: The walk takes roughly 30 to 45 minutes from the medina, mostly uphill on a stony path. Aim to arrive about an hour before sunset, so you can find a spot and watch the light turn the town from white to blue to gold. Bring a light jacket for the descent and a torch or phone light.

moods.title: What to Expect at the Spanish Mosque
moods.subtitle: A simple outing with a big view.

1.title: The Walk Up
1.desc: A steady, stony climb from the medina. It's not technical, but wear shoes with grip and bring water.

2.title: Sunset Over the Medina
2.desc: The blue town, the valley and the Rif in one frame. Arrive early to get a good spot.

3.title: Getting Back Down
3.desc: Leave while there is still light, or use a torch. Walk down in a group if you can.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Spanish Mosque (Bouzafar)

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: The path starts on the east side of the medina near the river. Ask your host or follow the signs and other walkers.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Aim to be at the top about an hour before sunset. Autumn and spring evenings are the most pleasant.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: There is no shop at the top, so bring water. Take a torch for the way down, and dress for cooler air.

q1.question: How long is the walk to the Spanish Mosque?
q1.answer: About 30 to 45 minutes uphill from the medina, so allow up to two hours round trip.

q2.question: Can you go inside the Spanish Mosque?
q2.answer: It is mainly visited for the view from outside and around it. Check locally if anything is open.

q3.question: Is the walk safe at sunset?
q3.answer: Many travellers do it, so you'll rarely be alone. Go with others, leave before dark and carry a torch.

q4.question: Is there an entrance fee?
q4.answer: No, it is a free outdoor viewpoint. Bring your own water and snacks.
